items.title: Kering has closed at least 217 stores over 18 months, more planned, as Gucci network shrinks
items.summary: Business outlet reports Kering finalized 84 net store closures in H1 2026 alone (part of a 100-closure full-year target), bringing total store count down to 1,635 from 1,719 at end-2025; over the trailing 18 months the group has shed at least 217 locations. Framed as deliberate rationalization under CEO Luca de Meo's ReconKering plan rather than distress, with Gucci bearing the largest share of closures.

items.source: HPCi Media (Home & Personal Care Middle East & Africa)
items.title: L'Oreal targets early-2028 debut for first Gucci Beauty products under accelerated license takeover
items.summary: Trade press reports Paris-based L'Oreal is targeting an early-2028 launch for its first Gucci Beauty products after accelerating its takeover of the fragrance and cosmetics license from Coty; Kering reportedly paid roughly 400 million dollars to redeem the existing Coty deal early. Positions beauty as a key future pillar of Gucci's European-anchored revenue diversification.

items.title: Bernstein analyst scores Demna's Gucci runway debut 7.6 out of 10, 'more good than bad'
items.summary: Milan-based luxury analyst Luca Solca of Bernstein gave Demna's fall 2026 Gucci runway debut a 7.6/10, calling it 'not a home run, but still an improvement' versus predecessor Sabato de Sarno's 6.8 debut, though behind rival debuts at Dior, Chanel, Loewe and Bottega Veneta. Notes jackets and trousers as solid, shoes and bags as uninteresting, and criticizes some looks as vulgar and the venue as excessive.

items.title: Gucci faces online backlash over AI-generated campaign images ahead of Demna's Milan debut
items.summary: Marketing-trade outlet reports Gucci's release of AI-generated advertising images ahead of Demna's runway debut triggered heavy criticism on social platforms for feeling impersonal and overproduced; commenters called the campaign cheap and tacky, with some threatening boycotts and framing AI use as incompatible with the artisanal-craft justification behind luxury pricing. Gucci did not publicly respond to comment requests, which reportedly deepened the backlash.

items.title: Trustpilot reviews of gucci.com continue to show a low aggregate rating dominated by service and quality complaints
items.summary: Consumer review aggregator shows gucci.com holding a low overall star rating, with recurring complaints about customer service responsiveness, delivery/returns handling, and product-quality issues such as hardware tarnishing or stitching defects after light use. Reviews are anonymous and unverified as purchases, so treated as opinion-thermometer signal only, not a verified quality audit.

items.title: PurseForum community reviews the Gucci Paparazzo bag as a versatile new-era staple
items.summary: Handbag-collector community coverage of the Paparazzo bag, one of the Demna-era leather goods credited by Kering with returning Gucci leather goods to growth, describes the leather as soft yet sturdy and the design as more versatile than prior seasons' releases; commenters are largely positive but several flag price-to-craftsmanship skepticism relative to competitor bags in the same bracket.

items.title: Gucci's official X account continues Summer 2026 campaign push around Lady Lunetta bag and Flora 60th anniversary
items.summary: Official brand channel activity promoting the second chapter of the Summer 2026 campaign and the new Lady Lunetta half-moon GG canvas bag, tied to the 60th anniversary of the Flora motif; owned-channel marketing content, discounted per sentiment-rubric treatment of brand-controlled activation versus independent public opinion.

items.title: Highsnobiety op-ed asks why fashion communities remain so polarized over Demna at Gucci
items.summary: Culture-and-streetwear outlet piece surveys online fan and critic reaction to Demna's Gucci appointment and debut, describing him as one of the industry's most polarizing figures; catalogs recurring community complaints that his Gucci looked derivative of his own Balenciaga/Vetements codes rather than distinctly Gucci, alongside a smaller camp praising the archive-referencing direction.
